title: FedPseudo: Privacy-Preserving Pseudo Value-Based Deep Learning Models for Federated Survival Analysis

problem.claim: Federated Survival Analysis must handle non-linear and non-IID client data distributions, censoring-induced bias, and privacy of shared information.

gap.claim: Existing work has adapted Cox Proportional Hazards models for FSA, but systematic exploration of these challenges is lacking.

contributions.claim: FedPseudo is a pseudo value-based deep learning framework for Federated Survival Analysis that learns representations from non-linear survival data and model parameters through federated learning.
The framework proposes an approach for estimating federated pseudo values and uses them to address non-uniform censoring.
The framework investigates differential privacy for federated pseudo values and local model updates and adapts V-Usable Information to quantify client-data informativeness.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their approach for estimating pseudo values for FSA as novel and simple.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that federated pseudo values are consistent and can be computed faster than traditional pseudo-value methods.
The authors report extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world survival datasets.
The authors report better performance than other FSA approaches, performance similar to the best centrally trained deep survival model, and consistently superior results across censoring settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Survival analysis supports patient care, and FSA applies federated learning to survival prediction across medical institutions while preserving privacy.
FSA faces non-linear, non-IID, and censoring-related challenges, while systematic investigation beyond CoxPH adaptations is lacking.
FedPseudo combines deep representations, pseudo values for non-uniform censoring, and federated parameter learning, including a new pseudo-value estimation approach.
The paper reports consistency of federated pseudo values, faster computation, differential-privacy investigations, and a client-data informativeness metric.
Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets are reported to show strong performance across FSA comparisons and censoring settings.

source_observation.claim: Combining pseudo values with federated learning is presented as a way to address censoring while learning from decentralized survival data.

interpretation.claim: A representation that makes censored outcomes more usable may complement distributed optimization when client data are heterogeneous.

application.claim: For decentralized time-to-event modeling, consider outcome transformations that explicitly account for censoring before federated aggregation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers to other event-time settings, data regimes, or privacy requirements.

unknowns: Specific datasets, sample sizes, and censoring rates
Model architectures, baselines, metrics, and numerical results
Differential-privacy mechanisms, budgets, and utility trade-offs
Assumptions and details of the consistency proof
